svg.text: Example: ServiceClient calls PaymentService | config: windowSize=10, failureThreshold=50%, successThreshold=2, openTimeoutMs=30000, halfOpenMaxCalls=3
SETUP – creating the circuit breaker (once, at application start)
INVOCATION – what happens inside every callRemote()
-> returned to ServiceClient: caller gets an answer, not an outage
allowRequest() by state: CLOSED = always true | OPEN = false until openTimeoutMs elapsed (then moves to HALF_OPEN) | HALF_OPEN = true only for the first halfOpenMaxCalls (3) probe calls
SLIDING WINDOW – the last 10 results live in a Deque<Boolean> (FIFO)
evict oldest S, add F -> TRIP!
recordSuccess() / recordFailure(): if (results.size() == windowSize) results.pollFirst(); results.addLast(true | false);
failureRate() = count(false) / results.size() * 100 (only judged once the window is full, so 1-2 early failures cannot trip it)
reset() = results.clear() (called when HALF_OPEN -> CLOSED, so old failures never count against a recovered service)
BREAKING AND RECOVERY – state timeline for the same example
any probe fails -> back to OPEN (timer restarts)
PaymentService now gets ZERO traffic, so it
can recover; callers fail in ~0 ms, no pile-up
through as probes; extra calls -> fallback
probe fails? -> OPEN again, timer restarts
normal traffic resumes, counting starts fresh

Legend: S = success, F = failure | green = CLOSED, red = OPEN, amber = HALF_OPEN | method names match the class diagram (CircuitBreaker, CircuitState, SlidingWindow, FallbackHandler, StateChangeListener)
